description: User entities and internal personnel must enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all administrative and remote console access.
User access permissions and administrative privileges must be formally reviewed on a quarterly basis by department managers.
Access rights of terminated employees and contractors must be revoked within 24 hours of separation.
Passwords must be a minimum of 14 characters in length with uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special symbols, expiring every 90 days.
All source code changes to production systems require independent peer code review and passing automated tests prior to deployment.
Development and testing environments are logically separated from the production environment, with no production data in test environments.
Emergency and scheduled changes must receive formal approval from the Change Approval Board (CAB) prior to release.
Customer data stored in databases and file storage must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or stronger encryption algorithms.
All data transmitted across public networks or between microservices must be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher.
Cryptographic keys are rotated at least annually and access to key management systems is restricted to authorized security administrators.
Security incidents must be identified, triaged, and communicated to affected customers and vendors within 72 hours of confirmation.
System, authentication, and application logs are centrally collected, retained for at least 365 days, and protected against unauthorized modification.
Full or incremental data backups must be performed daily, encrypted, and periodically tested for restorability.
Business continuity and disaster recovery plans must be tested at least annually to validate recovery time objectives (RTO).
User entity must annually obtain and review SOC 2 Type 2 reports and bridge letters for all critical cloud service providers and subservice organizations.
